name: edge
description: Module 23: load balancing and proxies — round robin, HTTP vs TCP health checks, the failover window and redispatch, X-Forwarded-For (append vs overwrite), PROXY protocol and its two mismatches, cookie vs source-hash stickiness, and a forward proxy with http_proxy / HTTP_PROXY / NO_PROXY

files./etc/haproxy/haproxy.cfg:
global
  log stdout format raw local0 info
  maxconn 2000

defaults
  mode http
  log global
  option httplog
  timeout connect 1s
  timeout client 10s
  timeout server 10s

# stats as CSV: curl "http://LB:8404/stats;csv"
frontend stats
  bind :8404
  stats enable
  stats uri /stats

# :80 round robin, HTTP health check (GET /health must return 200), adds X-Forwarded-For
frontend http_rr
  bind :80
  option forwardfor
  default_backend app_http
backend app_http
  balance roundrobin
  option httpchk GET /health
  http-check expect status 200
  default-server inter 500ms fall 2 rise 2
  server b1 198.18.233.11:8080 check
  server b2 198.18.233.12:8080 check
  server b3 198.18.233.13:8080 check

# :81 the same servers with a plain TCP check (a connect is all it tests)
frontend tcp_checked
  bind :81
  default_backend app_tcp
backend app_tcp
  balance roundrobin
  default-server inter 500ms fall 2 rise 2
  server b1 198.18.233.11:8080 check
  server b2 198.18.233.12:8080 check
  server b3 198.18.233.13:8080 check

# :82 cookie stickiness: HAProxy inserts SRV=<server>
frontend sticky
  bind :82
  default_backend app_cookie
backend app_cookie
  balance roundrobin
  cookie SRV insert indirect nocache
  default-server inter 500ms fall 2 rise 2
  server b1 198.18.233.11:8080 check cookie b1
  server b2 198.18.233.12:8080 check cookie b2
  server b3 198.18.233.13:8080 check cookie b3

# :83 source-IP hash
frontend srchash
  bind :83
  default_backend app_source
backend app_source
  balance source
  hash-type consistent
  default-server inter 500ms fall 2 rise 2
  server b1 198.18.233.11:8080 check
  server b2 198.18.233.12:8080 check
  server b3 198.18.233.13:8080 check

# :84 layer 4 (mode tcp) with PROXY protocol v1 to backends that expect it (port 9090)
frontend l4_proxyproto
  mode tcp
  option tcplog
  bind :84
  default_backend app_pp
backend app_pp
  mode tcp
  balance roundrobin
  server b1 198.18.233.11:9090 send-proxy check
  server b2 198.18.233.12:9090 send-proxy check
  server b3 198.18.233.13:9090 send-proxy check

# :85 misconfigured: PROXY protocol sent to backends that do not expect it
frontend l4_mismatch
  mode tcp
  option tcplog
  bind :85
  default_backend app_pp_wrong
backend app_pp_wrong
  mode tcp
  server b1 198.18.233.11:8080 send-proxy
  server b2 198.18.233.12:8080 send-proxy
  server b3 198.18.233.13:8080 send-proxy

# :86 like :80, plus retry a failed connection on another server
frontend http_redispatch
  bind :86
  default_backend app_redispatch
backend app_redispatch
  balance roundrobin
  option httpchk GET /health
  retries 2
  option redispatch 1
  default-server inter 500ms fall 2 rise 2
  server b1 198.18.233.11:8080 check
  server b2 198.18.233.12:8080 check
  server b3 198.18.233.13:8080 check

checks.name: round robin: once the health checks pass (rise 2 × inter 500 ms), 30 requests split 10/10/10; each backend sees the load balancer as its peer and the client only in X-Forwarded-For
run: for i in $(seq 50); do [ $(curl -s 'http://198.18.232.1:8404/stats;csv' | grep -cE ',(DOWN|DOWN [0-9]/[0-9]|UP [0-9]/[0-9]),') = 0 ] && break; sleep 0.2; done; curl -s 'http://198.18.232.1:8404/stats;csv' | cut -d, -f1,2,18 | grep -E 'app_http,b'; ${BIN}/edgelab hits -url http://198.18.232.1:80/ -n 30 -show 2

checks.name: health checks: b2's application breaks (its /health and its pages return 500) but the port stays open — the HTTP check takes b2 out within ~1 s; the TCP check on :81 keeps sending it a third of the traffic
run: ip netns exec nl-edge-b2 curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8080/admin/health?code=500; sleep 1.5; curl -s 'http://198.18.232.1:8404/stats;csv' | cut -d, -f1,2,18 | grep -E '(app_http|app_tcp),b2'; grep -o 'Server app_http/b2 is DOWN, reason: [^,]*, code: [0-9]*' ${EVIDENCE}/service-lb-haproxy.log | head -1; ${BIN}/edgelab hits -url http://198.18.232.1:80/?app=health -n 30; ${BIN}/edgelab hits -url http://198.18.232.1:81/?app=health -n 30; ip netns exec nl-edge-b2 curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8080/admin/health?code=200; for i in $(seq 50); do [ $(curl -s 'http://198.18.232.1:8404/stats;csv' | grep -cE ',(DOWN|DOWN [0-9]/[0-9]|UP [0-9]/[0-9]),') = 0 ] && break; sleep 0.2; done

checks.name: failover when a backend's host goes silent (DROP): on :80 the one request that lands on b3 waits out 4 connect timeouts (1 + retries 3, 1 s each) and gets a 503; on :86 'option redispatch' retries it on another server after one timeout — slow, but it succeeds
run: echo '--- :80, b3 starts to DROP at 1.5 s:'; ${BIN}/edgelab hits -url http://198.18.232.1:80/ -n 60 -interval 50ms -timeout 8s > ${EVIDENCE}/h.txt & H=$!; sleep 1.5; ip netns exec nl-edge-b3 iptables -I INPUT -p tcp --dport 8080 -j DROP; wait $H; sed 1d ${EVIDENCE}/h.txt; ip netns exec nl-edge-b3 iptables -D INPUT -p tcp --dport 8080 -j DROP; for i in $(seq 50); do [ $(curl -s 'http://198.18.232.1:8404/stats;csv' | grep -cE ',(DOWN|DOWN [0-9]/[0-9]|UP [0-9]/[0-9]),') = 0 ] && break; sleep 0.2; done; echo '--- :86, b3 starts to DROP at 1.5 s:'; ${BIN}/edgelab hits -url http://198.18.232.1:86/ -n 60 -interval 50ms -timeout 8s > ${EVIDENCE}/h.txt & H=$!; sleep 1.5; ip netns exec nl-edge-b3 iptables -I INPUT -p tcp --dport 8080 -j DROP; wait $H; sed 1d ${EVIDENCE}/h.txt; ip netns exec nl-edge-b3 iptables -D INPUT -p tcp --dport 8080 -j DROP; for i in $(seq 50); do [ $(curl -s 'http://198.18.232.1:8404/stats;csv' | grep -cE ',(DOWN|DOWN [0-9]/[0-9]|UP [0-9]/[0-9]),') = 0 ] && break; sleep 0.2; done; echo '--- haproxy log for the 503 (timers Tq/Tw/Tc/Tr/Ta, termination state):'; grep -E 'app_http/b3 .* 503 ' ${EVIDENCE}/service-lb-haproxy.log | tail -1 | cut -c1-140

checks.name: failover when the process is gone (RST): refusals are instant but HAProxy waits ~1 s between retries — 3 s then a 503 on :80; with redispatch on :86 nobody notices
run: echo '--- :80, b3 starts to REJECT at 1.5 s:'; ${BIN}/edgelab hits -url http://198.18.232.1:80/ -n 60 -interval 50ms -timeout 8s > ${EVIDENCE}/h.txt & H=$!; sleep 1.5; ip netns exec nl-edge-b3 iptables -I INPUT -p tcp --dport 8080 -j REJECT --reject-with tcp-reset; wait $H; sed 1d ${EVIDENCE}/h.txt; ip netns exec nl-edge-b3 iptables -D INPUT -p tcp --dport 8080 -j REJECT --reject-with tcp-reset; for i in $(seq 50); do [ $(curl -s 'http://198.18.232.1:8404/stats;csv' | grep -cE ',(DOWN|DOWN [0-9]/[0-9]|UP [0-9]/[0-9]),') = 0 ] && break; sleep 0.2; done; echo '--- :86, b3 starts to REJECT at 1.5 s:'; ${BIN}/edgelab hits -url http://198.18.232.1:86/ -n 60 -interval 50ms -timeout 8s > ${EVIDENCE}/h.txt & H=$!; sleep 1.5; ip netns exec nl-edge-b3 iptables -I INPUT -p tcp --dport 8080 -j REJECT --reject-with tcp-reset; wait $H; sed 1d ${EVIDENCE}/h.txt; ip netns exec nl-edge-b3 iptables -D INPUT -p tcp --dport 8080 -j REJECT --reject-with tcp-reset; for i in $(seq 50); do [ $(curl -s 'http://198.18.232.1:8404/stats;csv' | grep -cE ',(DOWN|DOWN [0-9]/[0-9]|UP [0-9]/[0-9]),') = 0 ] && break; sleep 0.2; done

checks.name: X-Forwarded-For: the client forges 6.6.6.6. HAProxy (option forwardfor) adds its own header line after it, nginx with $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for appends to it, nginx with $remote_addr overwrites it — only the entry your own proxy added can be trusted
run: for p in 80 8001 8000; do echo "--- :$p"; ${BIN}/edgelab hits -url http://198.18.232.1:$p/ -n 1 -show 1 -xff 6.6.6.6 | sed -n 2p; done

checks.name: PROXY protocol: :84 balances at layer 4 (mode tcp) — no HTTP headers are touched, so there is no X-Forwarded-For; the client address arrives in the PROXY header the load balancer writes before the first byte
run: ${BIN}/edgelab hits -url http://198.18.232.1:84/ -n 3 -show 3; echo '--- backend log:'; grep 'PROXY header' ${EVIDENCE}/service-b1-proxyproto.log | tail -1

checks.name: PROXY protocol mismatches: sent to a backend that does not expect it (:85), the backend reads 'PROXY TCP4 …' as a request line and answers 400; a client that skips the header to a backend that requires it is cut off
run:
echo '--- via :85 to plain backends:'; ${BIN}/edgelab raw -to 198.18.232.1:85 'GET / HTTP/1.1
Host: x

'; echo '--- straight to b1:9090:'; ${BIN}/edgelab raw -to 198.18.233.11:9090 'GET / HTTP/1.1
Host: x

'; grep 'instead of a PROXY header' ${EVIDENCE}/service-b1-proxyproto.log | tail -1 | cut -d' ' -f2-
expect_contains: sent "GET / HTTP/1.1" instead of a PROXY header — closing

checks.name: stickiness: a cookie jar alone changes nothing on :80; on :82 HAProxy sets SRV=<server> and every later request goes to that server; :83 hashes the source IP, so one client always lands on one backend — cookie or not
run: echo '--- :80 with cookies:'; ${BIN}/edgelab hits -url http://198.18.232.1:80/ -n 12 -cookies | sed 1d; echo '--- :82 without cookies:'; ${BIN}/edgelab hits -url http://198.18.232.1:82/ -n 12 | sed 1d; echo '--- :82 with cookies:'; ${BIN}/edgelab hits -url http://198.18.232.1:82/ -n 12 -cookies -show 2 | sed 1d; echo '--- :83 (source hash) without cookies:'; ${BIN}/edgelab hits -url http://198.18.232.1:83/ -n 12 | sed 1d; echo "--- the cookie HAProxy sets: $(curl -si http://198.18.232.1:82/ | grep -i '^set-cookie' | tr -d '\r')"

checks.name: forward proxy: curl uses http_proxy but ignores upper-case HTTP_PROXY (a CGI 'httpoxy' safeguard); Go's ProxyFromEnvironment honors both; NO_PROXY sends a host direct, unless a lower-case no_proxy is also set (curl reads that one first); CONNECT (-p) makes the proxy a blind tunnel that sees only host:port
run: echo "curl, http_proxy:          $(env -i PATH=$PATH http_proxy=http://198.18.232.1:3128 curl -s http://198.18.233.11:8080/)"; echo "curl, HTTP_PROXY:          $(env -i PATH=$PATH HTTP_PROXY=http://198.18.232.1:3128 curl -s http://198.18.233.11:8080/)"; echo "Go,   HTTP_PROXY:          $(env -i PATH=$PATH HTTP_PROXY=http://198.18.232.1:3128 ${BIN}/edgelab hits -env-proxy -url http://198.18.233.11:8080/ -n 1 -show 1 | sed -n 2p)"; echo "curl, http_proxy+NO_PROXY: $(env -i PATH=$PATH http_proxy=http://198.18.232.1:3128 NO_PROXY=198.18.233.11 curl -s http://198.18.233.11:8080/)"; echo "curl, no_proxy=other.example NO_PROXY=198.18.233.11: $(env -i PATH=$PATH http_proxy=http://198.18.232.1:3128 no_proxy=other.example NO_PROXY=198.18.233.11 curl -s http://198.18.233.11:8080/)"; echo "curl -p (CONNECT):         $(curl -s -p -x http://198.18.232.1:3128 http://198.18.233.12:8080/)"; echo '--- proxy log:'; tail -4 ${EVIDENCE}/service-lb-fproxy.log | cut -d' ' -f2-
expect_contains: Go,   HTTP_PROXY:            response 1: HTTP 200 backend=b1 peer=198.18.233.1:
